verdict.printed: Page 121 (signature B, p. 9, 'GRADVS PRIMI'): Latin continuation arguing that God makes even monolingual people wise, citing John 14:12, Matthew 17:19, Luke 17:6, Mark 16:17 and John 20:22, ending mid-word 'Qui crediderit & ba'
verdict.evidence: 'wise men and teachers from among those who know only their native mother tongue' translates 'Sapientes & Doctores ex iis, qui solam & vnicam callent linguam maternam' at the top of page 121, and the English ends 'Whoever believes and is ba', matching the page's last words 'Qui crediderit & ba' (p. 121). The only additions are short Latin notes, the gloss on Elohim, and a summary.

verdict.printed: Page 168 (Hyginus, Poeticon Astronomicon, Book II): the end of the Mastusius/Crater story, two footnotes (a: Ovid's Fasti; b: the reading Matusium vs. Mastusium), the section on the Southern Fish (Piscis Notius), and the start of the section on the five planets (Jupiter/Phaethon, Heraclides Ponticus, Prometheus)
verdict.evidence: 'he ordered Mastusius, along with the mixing bowl, to be cast into the sea' and 'One of these belongs to Jupiter, named Phaethon' are both printed on page 168. The only additions are short glosses, such as the note 'or Cup; the constellation Crater' and the gloss 'Book of Days' for Fasti.

verdict.printed: Page 93 is a blank ruled leaf. Its only text is the cut-off margin title 本草綱目拾遺 卷一 (Supplement to the Compendium of Materia Medica, vol. 1).
verdict.evidence: 'Essential Records of Herbal Foundations, Table of Contents, Volume One' renders page 93's margin title, but it works from a misread transcription and gets the title wrong. 'Table of Contents' and the summary's 'table of contents heading' describe nothing on page 93, which has no contents list.

verdict.printed: Page 122: the end of the previous section ('im Himmel wieder finden, wie Christus spricht: Wer sein Leben lieb hat…'), then the heading '38. Arbeit, Geiz und Vertrauen auf Gott.' and two paragraphs on work, free will, and the shepherd and the doctor, ending 'denn mit dem Weisen regiert Er'
verdict.evidence: 'find them again in heaven, as Christ speaks: He who loves his life will lose it' renders 'im Himmel wieder finden, wie Christus spricht' (p.140), and the body stops at 'for with the wise He rules', which is where page 140 ends. The only additions are short term notes (Kunst, Wunder Gottes, Doktor) and a meta line about the previous page.

verdict.printed: Page 278 (header 'Theologie Orphice.') ends the fourth proposition on God's infinite power and gives the fifth (God is always and everywhere, quoting Orpheus, Parmenides and Zoroaster) and the start of the sixth (God acts through his being), breaking off at 'Re-'.
verdict.evidence: 'Hence divine nature is named by Orpheus the infinite end' and 'Zoroaster touched upon this mystically... All things are born from one fire' both render text printed on page 278.

verdict.printed: Page 91 has the title 弄甌圖 (Illustration of Playing with Bowls) above a woodcut: an acrobat bends over two rows of small bowls on the ground, a seated dignitary with a female attendant sits by a screen, and a standing onlooker is near a balustrade with pine and garden rocks.
verdict.evidence: '# Illustration of Playing with Bowls' translates the title 弄甌圖 printed on page 91. The note describes only page 91's picture. Nothing comes from the cuju text on page 90 or the 吞劒圖 on page 92.

verdict.printed: Page 99 (Livre I, Chapitre XXVI): end of French note (2) ('imposante; s'il ne gouverne pas son corps avec calme...'), then notes (3) through (8), covering tse/tsing 'calme', Yen-tchu, naï-ho, thien-hia and the prince who loses his ministers and his states.
verdict.evidence: 'IN WHAT MANNER PRECAUTION MUST BE TAKEN, LEST a contract... can be rescinded' (CAUTELA L., Baldus, Bartolus) renders a Latin legal treatise that isn't printed on page 149, 150 or 151. Page 150 actually holds French commentary on Tao Te King chapter XXVI.

verdict.printed: Page 15 (Liber I) prints the first doubt (pepper and scammony), the second doubt (blood fever, Avicenna against Galen, with Averroes and Peter of Abano), and the start of the third doubt (Avicenna on Conium/hemlock).
verdict.evidence: 'Whence Serapio the Aggregator, in his book of questions' and 'wishing with lion-like tooth to tear apart Galen, the prin' are both printed on page 15. The English stops there, so the third doubt on page 15 ('Auctores medici in dictione Cicute... Conion... Arabes vero plures ipsum iusquiamum esse putant') is left out. The only additions are short glosses such as 'The Canon of Medicine' and 'yellow bile'.

verdict.printed: Page 79 has only the volume heading 農桑輯要卷第五 (Nong Sang Ji Yao, Volume 5). The other columns are blank.
verdict.evidence: 'Fundamentals of Agriculture and Sericulture, Volume 5' translates the heading 農桑輯要卷第五 printed on page 79. The summary only describes this title leaf.

verdict.printed: Page 33 (Theorica): the end of Chapter XX ('est natura de H. & E. in O....Tamen teneas secretum'), the italic heading of Chapter XXI on how the species of metals transmute themselves, and the Chapter XXI text on transmutation, created fire and composite fire, ending 'ignifica-'.
verdict.evidence: 'can metals, or their species, be transmuted?' renders 'utrum metalla vel species eorum possunt transmutari?' (p45), and 'which is ignifying, ignifiable, and ignited. And' matches the last line of p45 and its catchword 'ta. Et'. Pages 44 and 46 are the same scan of p32, so none of their text is in this English.

verdict.printed: Page 50 (header 'Aanmerkingen op 't Leven'): it finishes the argument that a round table and a square table rest on separate extended substances, gives the examples of iron and water, wine and wood, and a stake driven into a stream, and opens point II on God as extended ('wat zullen we zeggen, wanneer wy denken, dat hy diervoegen')
verdict.evidence: 'The lower end of a stake driven into a stream ... surrounded by earth' renders 'Het onderste end van een paal, in een stroom geheit ... met aarde omzet' (page 252). 'what shall we say when we consider that He in this way' ends where page 252 ends. The only thing added is the short summary paragraph, which names Pierre Bayle as the author even though his name is not printed on the page.

verdict.printed: Page 28: the volvelle diagram titled 'PRIMA PARS / Instrumentum Theoricæ Solis / AVX SOLIS', with zodiac and month rings, Vmbra Recta/Versa scales and an attached thread, and 'OPPOSITVM AVGIS' below
verdict.evidence: 'FIRST PART / Instrument for the Theory of the Sun / APOGEE OF THE SUN / OPPOSITE OF THE APOGEE' translate the headings printed on page 28. The note describes the diagram, and the summary and keywords are only short metadata, though the summary does not mention that the page title says 'First Part'.

verdict.printed: Running header 'Ms 2038 BIB. NAT. — FOLIO 7 (recto). —' and the bracketed title '[RAYONS VISUELS]' above a short rule; nothing else
verdict.evidence: '### Visual Rays.' translates '[RAYONS VISUELS]', printed on page 184. The header 'Ms 2038 National Library – Folio 7 (recto)' is also on page 184. Only the short summary sentence is extra.

verdict.printed: Page 69 (fo. xxiij, Liber primus): the end of the plague after David's census, quoting Augustine; Jeroboam's altars at Dan and Bethel, with the split altar and the withered hand; Uzzah's death beside the Ark; the heading of Chapter 7 on Elijah, the drought, the ravens and the widow; the opening of the Elijah narrative; and margin notes (Aug. ij. mirabilium lib., De hieroboam idolatria, and Sedulius verses).
verdict.evidence: 'Jeroboam son of Nebat, king of the ten tribes in the northern region' and 'Uzzah son of Abinadab followed the ark' render page 69 (Iheroboam filius Nabath... / Oza fili' Aminadab). One printed sentence on page 69 is left out: 'Ex quo (inquit Augustinus) intelligitur David minorem culpam commisisse quam plebs...' (Augustine: from this David is understood to have sinned less than the people). The only addition is a short note describing the woodcut initial.

verdict.printed: Page 6 has only a handwritten provenance note, 'Josiah H. Benton Fd / Dec. 16, 1942 / L', above an owner's mark of crossed tools in a circular patch; the rest is bleed-through from page 5.
verdict.evidence: 'Josiah H. Benton Fd / Dec. 16, 1942 / L' is written on page 6. The added summary and the keywords ('library acquisition', 'Josiah H. Benton Fund') are a little extra commentary. The note calls the mark a horizontal line over an inverted V, but the image shows crossed tools like the shield on page 5.

verdict.printed: Page 22 is Tibetan commentary on the request to explain the supreme secret practice. It covers Vairochana giving the Great Bliss vajra to Vajrasattva, the samadhi of the first vajra that arises from non-referential great compassion, and why the vajra was given (the realm of sentient beings).
verdict.evidence: 'It means, grant me the permission to explain the practice of Great Bliss Vajrasattva' renders the opening of page 22 (ཡང་གཞན་ལས་ཁྱད་པར་དུ་འཕགས་པས་ན་མཆོག...). The ending 'Regarding the intention of the realm of sentient beings without exception...' matches the last line of page 22 (...ལུས་པ་མེད་པའི་བསམ་). The only additions are short glosses and notes, such as the note on Vairochana as the central Buddha of the five families.

verdict.printed: Page 549 of the Libellus de Alchimia, in two columns. It covers how metals can be changed (copper and calamine, tin to litharge, iron to quicksilver, lead to white lead to red lead), the foundation of the art, and the first five precepts for the alchemist, ending with the warning about tinting without sublimation.
verdict.evidence: 'first in grindings, second in sublimations... they will neither penetrate nor mix with the bodies' renders the end of column 2 on page 555 ('primo in contributionibus... non ingredientur nec permiscentur corporibus'). The only additions are short glosses such as 'zinc ore' and 'lead monoxide'.

verdict.printed: Nothing is printed on page 30. It is a plain tan back cover or endpaper with thread stitching on the left edge, and it has no text or pictures.
verdict.evidence: The English says 'This leaf is blank and contains no printed text or illustrations.' That correctly describes page 30, and none of page 29's text appears in it.

verdict.printed: Page 326 (cols. 637–638) of Antonelli's preface: the end of the Theotokos argument (Nestorius, Dionysius, Alexander's letter, Athanasius' use of the term), then section XXXIV on the 'for the octave' psalm titles (Barnabas, Irenaeus, list of Fathers, James of Nisibis), ending with Gennadius' words 'in libro Χρονικῶν ... quos', plus footnotes 77–85
verdict.evidence: 'argued the ignorance of Nestorius, who rejected this term Theotokos' and 'Hippolytus in Photius ... in the book of the *Chro' are both printed on page 326; the bracketed notes render that page's footnotes 77–85. The only additions are short glosses such as 'God-bearer, Mother of God', which are not printed on page 326

verdict.printed: Page 80 (p. 59) has the running header 'LIVRE III.', a faint plate label '[Planche] VIII' and two pictures: a ground plan of the temple in antis and a front view of it with a double pediment, two columns and pilasters.
verdict.evidence: 'BOOK III.' and 'Pl. VIII' translate the header and plate label printed on page 80; the note describing a 'ground plan' and a 'pedimented portico supported by columns and pilasters' matches the two pictures on page 80. Nothing is taken from the text on pages 79 or 81.

verdict.printed: Header 'DE ARTE CABALISTICA' and 42 lines of Hebrew psalm verses containing the Tetragrammaton, ending with Genesis 1:1, plus the catchword אודה
verdict.evidence: The English renders every Hebrew line printed on page 155, from 'Behold, God is my helper' to 'In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth'. The only addition is a short summary, which counts as minor.

verdict.printed: Page 255 (Gogol's 'Заколдованное мѣсто', the enchanted-spot story): grandfather takes a pinch of snuff, something sneezes overhead, he digs up a cauldron, and a bird's beak, a ram's head and a bear mock his words, ending with «Сло-»; signature line 'ТОМЪ I. 29'.
verdict.evidence: 'horn, poured snuff onto his fist ... "Terrifying to say a word!" bleated the ram's head. "A wo-' matches page 469 from «рожокъ, насыпалъ на кулакъ табаку» to «Сло-». The only additions are in the metadata: the keyword 'Evenings on a Farm Near Dikanka' and the summary's 'in the woods' and 'forest creatures'. None of these are printed on the page.

verdict.printed: Running head 'Splendor Solis.' and page number 45, the heading 'Figur.', a hand-coloured woodcut of a sun with a face rising over mountains, a walled city, a river, a castle and a traveller gesturing toward the sun, decorative borders, signature 'F iij' and catchword 'Von'
verdict.evidence: '# Figure.' renders the heading 'Figur.' printed on page 295, and the note describes page 295's woodcut (sun with a face, walled city, river, traveller with a pack). Nothing comes from page 294's fourth article or page 296's text on the governing of the fire.

verdict.printed: Page 176 has the running header 'DE PHILIBERT DE L'ORME.', the page number 84, the signature 'p ij', and a full-page stereotomy diagram with arcs numbered 1–6, the letters I, S, B and F, and a small lower-left inset numbered 1–4.
verdict.evidence: 'BY PHILIBERT DE L'ORME.' and 'p ij' are the header and signature printed on page 176; the note describes page 176's diagram, including the arcs numbered 1 through 6 and the shaded section marked F. Only the page number 84 is left out.

verdict.printed: Page 36 (printed p. 32) has the header 'LIBRO' and a full-page engraving of an Ionic base and pedestal. The engraving carries letter labels A–L, measurements in minutes, 'Modulo I minuti 22 ½' across the die, 'Modulo I minuti 35' running vertically, and a scale bar.
verdict.evidence: 'Module 1, 22 ½ minutes' and 'Module 1, 35 minutes' translate the inscriptions printed on the pedestal die on page 36. The only additions are short glosses such as 'standard unit of measurement' and a summary and keywords line, none of which is printed on any page.

verdict.printed: Page 141 is a hand-coloured plate headed 'No. 54.' and 'Opus Mag. Cab. ii.'. It shows a hexagram ringed by seven planet discs, joined to a set of concentric rings labelled SERAPHIM, CHERVBIM, THRONI, DOMINATIONES, PRINCIPATVS, POTESTATES, VIRTVTES, ARCHANGELI, ANGELI and MVNDVS INTELLIGENTIARVM, with letter markers B–Y.
verdict.evidence: The labels 'SERAPHIM… POWERS' and the heading 'Magical-Cabbalistic Work, Part II' come from page 141. The English leaves out VIRTVTES, ARCHANGELI, ANGELI, MVNDVS INTELLIGENTIARVM and 'No. 54'. It also adds a page number '153' and a note describing faint bleed-through and a red stamp, which both belong to page 140. Each order gets a background gloss, such as 'burning ones who surround the divine throne', and none of these glosses are printed on any of the three pages.

verdict.printed: Page 316 is a section title page printed with only "LESARTEN. TEXT." and the Google digitization watermark.
verdict.evidence: "# READINGS. TEXT." translates the heading "LESARTEN. TEXT." printed on page 316. Nothing is taken from Flügel's preface on page 315 or from the blank page 317.

verdict.printed: Page 116 is the closing line of the volume, 營造法式卷三 (Yingzao Fashi, Volume Three). The rest of the leaf is blank ruled columns, with a cut-off margin note reading 卷三.
verdict.evidence: 'Building Standards, Volume Three' renders 營造法式卷三, which is printed on page 116. The summary only describes that title and adds no new content.

verdict.printed: Page 49 opens Caput III, 'De nominibus Firmamenti, et signis eius, et impressionibus eius': Coptic, Latin and Arabic columns for Cæli, Cælum Cælorum, Abyss, Apogeum, the firmament, the seven planets (Sol, Luna, Saturnus, Iuppiter, Mars, Venus, Mercurius), Astra, and Signa Zodiaci duodecim, with catchword ⲕⲣⲓⲟⲥ.
verdict.evidence: 'The Pleiades, or the Hyades, the Hen of Heaven; this is a station of the Moon in Taurus' and the other lunar-mansion entries (Aldebaran, Gemini, Leo) are not printed on page 106 (p.49), page 105 (p.48, angels) or page 107 (p.50, zodiac signs and the first mansions). They follow the transcription, which describes a later page (p.51).

verdict.printed: Epigraph headed 'Syr. Cap. IV. v. 12.13.' quoting Sirach on wisdom exalting her children and giving great joy to those who seek her; bleed-through of the title page is visible from the other side.
verdict.evidence: 'Wisdom exalts her children, and readily welcomes those who seek her' renders the Sirach quotation printed on page 238; the note on modern verse numbering (4:11–12) is an added gloss.

verdict.printed: Page 3 (POLIPHILE., sig. A iij): Poliphile chases the moving voice, loses the fountain, and collapses exhausted under an ancient oak (woodcut); he remembers Circe's enchantments and wonders how he could find moly, ending 'mais qu'est ce dōc'
verdict.evidence: 'at the foot of a very ancient oak, which cast shade upon a green meadow' and 'how shall I be able here among so many kinds of herbs to find moly' render page 22's printed text. The only additions are the gloss 'the mythical herb of Hermes', the note on 'la mercuriale', and the summary and keywords, none of which are printed on any of the three pages.

verdict.printed: Page 61 has the title 坐罾 (stationary dip net), a woodcut of a fisherman on a platform under a willow working a lever-and-pulley dip net, and the margin text 三才圖會 器用五卷 with a leaf number.
verdict.evidence: 'Stationary Dip Net' renders the title 坐罾 printed on page 61, and 'Collected Illustrations of the Three Realms, Utensils, Volume 5' renders the margin text 三才圖會 器用五卷 on page 61. The willow and platform description matches the picture on page 61.

verdict.printed: Page 362 has only the closing line 沖虛至德眞經解卷之五終 (end of juan 5 of the Explanation of the Chongxu Zhide Zhenjing) on a ruled leaf that is otherwise empty, and the facing leaf is blank.
verdict.evidence: 'End of Volume Five of the Explanation of the True Scripture of Perfect Virtue and Emptiness' translates 沖虛至德眞經解卷之五終, which is printed on page 362.

verdict.printed: Page 382 is the blank back of the plate. The only marks are faint, mirrored show-through of plate Tab. I's diagrams from page 381, with no text of its own.
verdict.evidence: The English is a description written for the page ('five circular astronomical and geometric diagrams… a hexagram inscribed in a circle'), not a rendering of anything printed. Those shapes are show-through from page 381. The summary also adds an unsupported claim, 'plate 17, intended for page 117', which comes from the transcription's uncertain margin reading and is not legibly printed on any of the three pages.

verdict.printed: Half-title page: 'ORBIS SENSUALIUM PICTUS. A World of Things Obvious to the Senses drawn in Pictures.' between rows of printer's ornaments, page number (15)
verdict.evidence: The errata list ('tumditur', 'Funditur 109', 'galeam, 186', 'bombardica, 282') is printed on page 24. The 'or } line 9. 26' meta note and the summary, which present it as Hoole's errata, are added commentary. Page 25's title is not rendered anywhere.
